wave.summary: Added one table-driven test ('every successful invocation mode writes nothing to stderr') covering all five success modes (default, --compact, --block, --json, --help) in a single test with a loop, per the item's own judgment note that one test closing a named surface beats several restating existing passes — the five modes share one behavioral claim (silent stderr + exit 0 on success), so splitting them into five tests would just be churn. Used spawnSync directly (never execFileSync's throw path, never a shell pipe) per playbook L-010, reading .status and .stderr directly. Each mode asserts BOTH exit status 0 and stderr === '' so a mode that silently exits non-zero with empty stderr cannot read as a pass. Confirmed pre-existing gap first: grepped the file and verified run() calls execFileSync with no stdio override, so stderr was inherited by the parent test process on every prior passing-path test, making REPORT.md's 'nothing on stderr on success' claim genuinely untested before this change. Did not touch package.json, bin/, src/, or REPORT.md.
